title: Fix missing libonnxruntime.so symlink in Linux prebuilt fallback
description: The v0.1.0 moonshine-voice-linux-x86_64.tar.gz / -linux-arm64.tar.gz release archives only ship the versioned SONAME libonnxruntime.so.1 (confirmed via objdump - it is also the DT_NEEDED entry baked into libmoonshine.so, so it's correct at runtime via the existing -Wl,-rpath flag). But build.rs's Linux fallback branch emits cargo:rustc-link-lib=dylib=onnxruntime, which makes the linker search for the unversioned libonnxruntime.so, which doesn't exist in the archive, causing 'cannot find -lonnxruntime' at link time. This was previously masked because CI never got past the Tauri WebKitGTK pkg-config failure to reach the link step. Fix: create a libonnxruntime.so -> libonnxruntime.so.1 symlink in the extracted lib dir during download_prebuilt_release() when missing.

title: Support downloading prebuilt libmoonshine release assets in moonshine-sys build.rs
description:
Currently `crates/moonshine-sys/build.rs` requires a local clone of moonshine-ai/moonshine (via `MOONSHINE_DIR` or relative-path search) and compiles libmoonshine from source via CMake. While functional, this is a heavyweight prerequisite for a `cargo add moonshine-rs` user.

Official moonshine-ai/moonshine GitHub releases already publish prebuilt, ready-to-link binaries for every tagged version (verified against v0.0.73):
- `moonshine-voice-macos-arm64.tar.gz`: universal (arm64+x86_64) `libmoonshine.a` with ONNX Runtime statically merged in (confirmed via nm: `_OrtGetApiBase` is a defined symbol).
- `moonshine-voice-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` / `moonshine-voice-linux-arm64.tar.gz`: `libmoonshine.so` + `libonnxruntime.so.1`.
- `moonshine-voice-windows-x86_64.tar.gz`: `moonshine.lib`, `bin-tokenizer.lib`, `ort-utils.lib`, `moonshine-utils.lib`, `onnxruntime.lib`/`.dll`.
- Every archive includes `include/moonshine-c-api.h`, the exact header `bindgen` needs.

Proposal:
Add an opt-in `build.rs` path (mirroring the `download-binaries` feature in the real `ort-sys` crate — see its `build/download/` module for the implementation pattern: fetch via an HTTP client, verify checksum, extract) that:
1. Resolves a target moonshine release tag (pinned version or latest).
2. Downloads the matching platform archive from `https://github.com/moonshine-ai/moonshine/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>.tar.gz`.
3. Extracts it into `OUT_DIR` and links directly, skipping CMake compilation for that path.
4. Falls back to (or is gated alongside) the existing `MOONSHINE_DIR` source-build path for unsupported platforms or local development.

This removes the 'clone the whole moonshine monorepo' requirement for common cases, consistent with how `ort-sys` behaves in the wider Rust ecosystem.

title: Enable word timestamps via TranscriberOptions::with_word_timestamps + model fetch
description:
Enable word-level timestamps through the safe API. Verified end-to-end during DevRel research.

ROOT CAUSE (two requirements; one currently impossible via the safe API):
1. The model directory must contain decoder_with_attention.ort (non-streaming) — published for 'en'. It is added to the manifest only when word_timestamps=true (confirmed: get_stt_dependencies_with_options('en', with_arch(Tiny).with_word_timestamps(true)) lists decoder_with_attention.ort, ~30MB, roughly doubles the download). C API refs: vendor/moonshine-c-api.h lines 431-433 and 1024-1028.
2. word_timestamps=true must be passed as a LOAD option to moonshine_load_transcriber_from_files. GAP: with_word_timestamps() exists only on SttDependenciesOptions (manifest resolution), NOT on TranscriberOptions (load). Today the only way is the generic escape hatch TranscriberOptions::new().set("word_timestamps", "true").

PROVEN: with decoder_with_attention.ort present AND .set("word_timestamps","true") passed to from_files, TranscriptLine.words populates correctly (e.g. 12 words on line 1 of two_cities_16k.wav, each with start/end/confidence).

NOTE: identify_speakers=true auto-enables word timestamps (header line 187/219).
acceptance_criteria:
1. TranscriberOptions gains with_word_timestamps(bool) that sets the 'word_timestamps' load key (mirrors the .set escape hatch).
2. download_model example gains a flag/arg to also fetch decoder_with_attention.ort via SttDependenciesOptions::with_word_timestamps(true).
3. word_timestamps example calls .with_word_timestamps(true) and its 'no words' hint is updated to mention both the attention file and the load option.
4. rustdoc on with_word_timestamps and TranscriptWord notes the file + option requirement; user-guide documents that identify_speakers also auto-enables word timestamps.
5. Verified: running the word_timestamps example against a model dir containing decoder_with_attention.ort prints per-word start/end/confidence.

title: SpeakerSpan char ranges return 0/0 (unknown) in batch mode; document + fix example slicing
description:
CORRECTION: the earlier 'document-global' observation was wrong. Per the C API header (vendor/moonshine-c-api.h lines 230-236 and 270-272), SpeakerSpan.start_char/end_char are UTF-8 BYTE offsets into the LINE's text, clipped to the line's time range (i.e. line-relative), and are documented as BOTH ZERO when unknown.

ACTUAL RUNTIME FINDING (batch/non-streaming, tiny-en + identify_speakers=true against test-assets/endgame_nagg_nell.wav): every span returns start_char=0, end_char=0 (= unknown). speaker_index and timing (start_time/duration) are correct; only the character ranges are absent. This is why the speaker_diarization example produced empty text snippets.

IMPACT: the current speaker_diarization example attempts to byte-slice line.text using 0/0 offsets, yielding empty snippets. It also has a latent bug: it slices by BYTE offset without checking char boundaries, which could panic if offsets were populated with multi-byte UTF-8.

OPEN QUESTION: determine whether char ranges are ever populated (e.g. streaming mode via moonshine_transcribe_stream, and/or when word_timestamps is explicitly enabled). Header line 219 says word_timestamps auto-enables with diarization, but ranges were still 0/0 here — worth testing streaming.
acceptance_criteria:
1. SpeakerSpan rustdoc states: start_char/end_char are line-relative UTF-8 BYTE offsets, and 0/0 means 'unknown/unpopulated'.
2. speaker_diarization example no longer attempts to slice when offsets are 0/0; it prints speaker index + timing, and only shows a text range when offsets are non-zero, using byte-safe slicing (str::get on byte range) that cannot panic.
3. Investigation note recorded (comment or user-guide) on whether streaming mode populates char ranges; if it does, document the difference.
4. Verified against endgame_nagg_nell.wav (2 speakers): output is clean with no empty-bracket snippets.

title: Support true real-time streaming transcription across FFI, Rust wrapper, and Tauri demo
description:
Currently moonshine-sys and moonshine-rs bind only the non-streaming batch transcription C API (moonshine_transcribe_without_streaming). The mic-recorder component in demo/tauri-mic-transcriber uses periodic batch transcription calls as a interim progressive update mechanism.

To support true low-latency real-time streaming speech recognition across the stack:
1. moonshine-sys: Bind C API streaming functions (moonshine_create_stream, moonshine_free_stream, moonshine_start_stream, moonshine_stop_stream, moonshine_transcribe_add_audio_to_stream, moonshine_transcribe_stream).
2. moonshine-rs: Expose safe Stream struct with methods for adding chunk audio and retrieving partial/final transcripts.
3. demo/tauri-mic-transcriber: Update mic-recorder to send real-time 100ms-200ms audio chunks to a persistent Tauri stream handle and emit transcript line updates to the Lit frontend.

title: Track additional libmoonshine C API surfaces (intent recognizer, TTS/G2P, transcript_to_string, memory-file loading)
description:
Discovered while researching the C API header (vendor/moonshine-c-api.h). libmoonshine exposes substantial functionality not yet wrapped by moonshine-rs. Catalog for future work / prioritization:

INTENT RECOGNIZER (lines ~674-825): moonshine_create_intent_recognizer[_from_memory], register/unregister_intent, get_closest_intents, get_intent_count, clear_intents, calculate_intent_embedding, calculate_embedding_distance, free_intent_matches/embedding. Embedding arch: GEMMA_300M. Has its own get_intent_dependencies manifest.

TEXT-TO-SPEECH / G2P (lines ~872-1003): create_tts_synthesizer_from_files/memory, free_tts_synthesizer, get_g2p_dependencies, get_tts_dependencies, get_tts_voices. Engines: Kokoro, Piper, ZipVoice (zero-shot cloning). Overlaps existing TTS roadmap.

SPEECH CLIPS (lines ~827-870): moonshine_extract_speech_clip + moonshine_speech_clip_t (VAD-based clip extraction for voice cloning reference; no model download needed).

DEBUG / LOADING HELPERS: moonshine_transcript_to_string (line 320, quick debug formatting), moonshine_load_transcriber_from_memory_files (line 452, bundled/in-memory models by canonical filename — already on roadmap).

Suggested next step: split into per-surface epics when prioritized (intent recognition likely a standalone epic; TTS folds into the existing TTS roadmap; transcript_to_string + speech clips are small, high-value adds).
acceptance_criteria: This is a tracking/triage task. Done when: (a) each surface above has been triaged (in-scope vs out-of-scope), and (b) in-scope surfaces have follow-up epics/tasks created.
close_reason: Triaged: Created follow-up tasks for in-memory loading (P2), Text Embedding API (P3), and TTS/Voice Synthesis API (P3).
